solutions.check: 32 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Fish-eater's oversize – kill!

blocks.note: OS is the clothing-label abbreviation for outsize
a kill is the prey an animal has caught

explanation.surface: A cry from someone watching an oversized fish-eater pounce on its catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but is really 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'kill' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a bird of prey that lives almost entirely on fish.

clue.text: Plastic pipes: too contrary

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters can be reshaped

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A plumber grumbling that plastic pipes are too awkward to work with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like the material the pipes are made of, but it is the instruction to remould the next letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary and opposite both mean facing the other way.

clue.text: OAP in trouble – but upright?

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: OAP (old-age pensioner) plus IN, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A pensioner has had a fall, yet somehow is still standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of 'in trouble' but is fodder. An upright is a piano whose strings run vertically, as opposed to a grand.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright is the everyday name for a vertical piano.

clue.text: Organ on creepy type that sticks in your head

definitions.text: Organ on creepy type that sticks in your head

blocks.note: the ear is an organ
a worm is a creepy-crawly and a creep

explanation.surface: A horror-film image of something crawling into a body part and lodging in the brain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts EAR above WORM. The whole clue also describes the answer: a tune that gets into your ear and won't leave.
explanation.definitionFit: An earworm is a catchy tune that keeps replaying in your head.

clue.text: Extensive cock up with Oasis concert initially

indicators.note: to cock something up is to mess it up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: used as it stands
used as it stands
first letter of concert

explanation.surface: A review complaining that an Oasis gig was a huge mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cock up' reads as one phrase, but 'cock' is the jumbling instruction and 'up' is among the letters jumbled. Oasis are a British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spacious is extensive, with plenty of room.

clue.text: God welcomes a good heathen!

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
used as it stands
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A charitable deity opening his arms to an unbeliever.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a god should welcome a heathen at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan is a heathen, someone outside the main religions.

clue.text: Body calling for new cash point on island

indicators.note: a new version of the word is a remade one, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: CASH rearranged
S (south) is a compass point
IS is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A person demanding fresh money from a cash machine on holiday somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cash point' reads as a cash machine, but splits into 'cash' to rearrange and 'point', a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the chassis is a car's body frame, the part everything else is bolted to.

clue.text: Topless at the Commons, everybody welcome?

blocks.note: without a top, like an open-topped car
the Commons is the lower House of the UK Parliament

explanation.surface: A scandal: someone baring all in the House of Commons, and nobody objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' suggests nudity but means only uncovered. The House of Commons is the elected chamber of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: An open house is an event where everybody is welcome to drop in.

clue.text: Just a couple of drops of semen and boyfriend gets to relax!

indicators.text: Just a couple of drops of
indicators.note: only two drops are taken, so only the first two letters

blocks.clueFragment: Just a couple of drops of semen
blocks.note: the first two letters of semen
a date is someone you are going out with

explanation.surface: A saucy line about a boyfriend unwinding after sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relax' is transitive here: to sedate someone is to relax them.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate someone is to relax them, usually with a drug.

clue.text: Large expanse ripe for development — look into it

blocks.note: RIPE rearranged
an air is a look or manner

explanation.surface: An estate agent's pitch for a big plot of land waiting to be built on: take a look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look into it' reads as an invitation to investigate; 'it' points back to the rearranged letters, and the look splits them after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: North America's grassland plains stretch for hundreds of miles.

clue.text: Emission – tax to the limit

definitions.note: 'Emission' is a noun and 'tax to the limit' a verb phrase; EXHAUST serves as both.

blocks.note: the fumes a car's engine gives out
a verb: to drain or use up completely

explanation.surface: A complaint about a pollution levy set as high as it can go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax' looks like a levy on emissions but is a verb: to tax to the limit is to wear out.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaust is both the fumes a vehicle emits and a verb meaning to drain completely.

clue.text: Enterprising energy chief hoarding top grade

indicators.note: to hoard is to keep something inside

blocks.note: go means energy or drive
a head is a chief
A is the top exam grade

explanation.surface: A business profile of a dynamic head of an energy company who keeps the best marks for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy chief' reads as the boss of a power company, but the two words are separate pieces that hold the grade between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an enterprising person pushes ahead with new ventures.

clue.text: Vote for manual workers' demo?

blocks.note: a vote taken by raising hands
hands are manual workers, and a demo is a show

explanation.surface: A union meeting deciding whether factory workers should go on a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'demo' looks like a street protest but is taken as a demonstration, a showing; 'hands' are labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a vote counted by raised hands, and literally a display by hands, the old word for labourers.

clue.text: (& 24ac.) Latest broadcast: politician's pretentious talk?

blocks.note: hot news is the latest
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A headline about the newest broadcast of a politician's empty speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two grid entries, the second at 24; 'broadcast' is a verb here, not the noun it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air is empty, boastful talk, the stock in trade of politicians.

clue.text: A short time taken by Hunt, yet devastated an English region

indicators.note: devastation leaves things in ruins, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: HUNT YET rearranged
a mo is a moment

explanation.surface: News that a politician named Hunt had a brief spell in office and wrecked part of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunt is the surname of more than one Conservative minister, which makes it look like a name to keep. Tynemouth is a town and borough at the mouth of the River Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tynemouth is a coastal area of north-east England.

clue.text: Disreputable, negative rubbish about acknowledgements of liability

indicators.note: turned about, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: no is a negative answer
rot means nonsense, rubbish
an IOU (I owe you) is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: A damning report on a shady firm's refusal to own up to its debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', linking the rubbish to the IOUs, but it tells you to turn the rubbish round.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous for something bad, disreputable.

clue.text: Commonplace stink associated with bass?

blocks.note: a hum is a bad smell
a bass drum is the big drum of a kit; 'perhaps' is signalled by the question mark

explanation.surface: A dull joke about the smell of a fish, the bass.
explanation.walkthrough: Bass reads as the fish, which fits 'stink', but it is the musical sense: a bass drum. 'Hum' for a smell is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something humdrum is dull and ordinary, as commonplace things are.

clue.text: Thus having an erection for a starter?

blocks.note: so means thus
the obvious slang sense

explanation.surface: A smutty joke about a man aroused before things have properly begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A starter' reads as a beginning, but it is the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: soup is one of the dishes served as a first course.

clue.text: Last composed Don't Panic

blocks.note: to last is to stay the course, endure
composed means calm

explanation.surface: A note that 'Don't Panic' was the final thing someone wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last composed' suggests a final composition, or 'composed' as an anagram sign for LAST; both are false, since STAY and CALM are plain synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Stay calm is the direct instruction 'don't panic'.

clue.text: Butt, bust operated on

indicators.note: surgery rearranges things, so the letters are moved about

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cosmetic-surgery tally: bottom and chest both done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' and 'bust' look like two body parts on a surgeon's list; butt is the definition, in its sense of a stub.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the smoker's sense: the leftover end of a cigarette.

clue.text: Crass ex-PM, ball trapped, needs hospital

blocks.note: Boris Johnson, former UK prime minister
O is round, like a ball
H is the map-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Tabloid gloating that a boorish former prime minister has hurt his groin and needs treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The ball goes after the B: B(O)ORIS. Boris Johnson was UK prime minister from 2019 to 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Boorish means crass and ill-mannered.

clue.text: Bloated corporation at end of the trail

blocks.note: a corporation is an old joke word for a pot belly
last letter of 'the'
a scent is the trail a hound follows

explanation.surface: A swipe at a fat company reaching the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a company, but it is dated British humour for a large belly, as is TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tumescent is the medical word for swollen.

clue.text: Sneak dick between legs, perhaps

blocks.note: LEGS rearranged
a dick is a fool, and so is a mug

explanation.surface: A crude image of someone hiding something between their thighs to get it past customs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dick' reads as anatomy, but it is the insult: a dick and a mug are both idiots. 'Perhaps' looks like hedging but marks the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to sneak goods past a border is to get them through illicitly.

clue.text: Scandalous affair material

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is palm fibre used as a material for weaving and tying.

Chance of corrupted input, or typo?

clue.text: Prized example of peer under pressure

clue.text: Archer happy to get this meal when ditching date?

clue.text: How an habitual drinker appears to gain one state

clue.text: Mobile meant to suppress a German tone

clue.text: Seat from where many a politician's speech originates?

definitions.text: Seat from where many a politician's speech originates?

blocks.note: the surface wants a seat in Parliament; the setter means the seat you sit on, the backside

blocks.clueFragment: from where many a politician's speech originates?
blocks.note: the jibe is that politicians talk out of their backsides, spouting nonsense

explanation.surface: A question about which parliamentary seat a politician's speeches come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' looks like a constituency, but it is the bottom; 'talking out of your arse' is British slang for spouting nonsense.

clue.text: Ultimately, Senator Vance acted weird for a celebrated winner

indicators.note: take only the last letter of each word

blocks.note: last letters of Senator, Vance, acted
rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: A jab at JD Vance for behaving oddly in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird' looks like part of the run of final letters, but is RUM. Red Rum was a racehorse that won the Grand National, Britain's great steeplechase, three times.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Rum is the most celebrated winner in Grand National history.
